q: Large multicellular animals have evolved transport system as organisms get larger and have higher ____ rates.
e: Higher metabolic rates in large animals necessitate an efficient mass transport system.

q: In many large animals, including all the vertebrates, circulatory system is in the form of ____ transport system.
e: Mass transport systems move substances rapidly in a fluid medium over long distances.

q: Mass transport system is an arrangement of structures by which substances are transported in the flow of a ____ with a mechanism for moving it around the body.
e: Blood or hemolymph acts as the fluid medium in mass transport systems.
A high surface area to volume ratio allows single-celled organisms to rely solely on diffusion.

q: In large multicellular organisms, the surface area to volume ratio is ____.
e: A low surface area to volume ratio means diffusion alone is too slow to supply internal cells.

q: These cells require a supply of chemical substances such as glucose and oxygen for ____.
e: Cellular respiration requires a continuous supply of oxygen and glucose to produce energy.

q: Respiration supplies energy for the other reactions of life, but it also produces the toxic waste product ____.
e: Carbon dioxide is a toxic waste product of aerobic respiration that must be removed.

q: Most mass transport systems have certain similar features as follow: ____ surfaces to get materials into and out of the transport system.
e: Exchange surfaces, like lungs or gills, allow materials to enter and leave the transport fluid.

q: a way of moving materials fast enough to supply the needs of the organism - this may involve mechanical methods such as the pumping of the ____.
e: The heart acts as a mechanical pump to maintain the flow of the transport medium.
A liquid transport medium is required to dissolve and carry substances.
